problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ -9 & 4\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{17}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}} & \frac{4}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A,$ $Σ,$ and $V$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ what is the first column of $U?$

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A,$ $Σ,$ and $V$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ what is the first column of $U?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ and ${\sigma }_{i}\ne 0,$ then the $i$th column of $U$ can be found as

$$
{u}_{i}=\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{i}}A{v}_{i},
$$

 

where ${v}_{i}$ is the $i$th column of the matrix $V.$

From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that the singular values are ${\sigma }_{1}=4$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=1.$ Therefore, the first column of $U$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{1}}A{v}_{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{8}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
